promises.d: A 03:40 landing is a normal pickup time here, not a problem to solve at the desk. The name is the opening hours, not a slogan.
Twenty cars, each one photographed and priced on its own page. You book that car, not a category with 'or similar' printed next to it.
Collect at arrivals, drop in town. Two locations, ten minutes apart, no fee for using both.
Nineteen of the twenty cars are automatic, which matters on Albanian mountain roads more than anywhere you have driven before.
One number, answered by someone in Tirana who can move a car. Not a queue, not a chatbot.

faq.q: How do I book a car?
faq.a: Send us the dates, the car you want and your flight number by WhatsApp or phone. We reply with a written confirmation on WhatsApp. There is no account to create.

faq.q: Is there a deposit?
faq.a: Any deposit is settled at the office when you collect, and nothing is charged in advance through this website. The amount, and whether it is cash or a card hold, depends on the car, so ask us when you send your dates and we will confirm it in writing with the total before you travel.

faq.q: Do I pay online?
faq.a: No. Nothing is charged in advance and no card details are taken through this website. You settle at pickup, once you have seen the car.

faq.q: Is the price per day the final price?
faq.a: The rates on this site are our daily rates, per car, in euro. Ask us for the total for your exact dates and we will send it to you in writing before you commit to anything.

faq.q: Is it cheaper for a longer rental?
faq.a: Usually yes. The daily rate comes down as the rental gets longer, so send us your dates and we will work out the total for you.

faq.q: Can I change or cancel?
faq.a: Plans move, especially with flights. Tell us as early as you can by WhatsApp and we will confirm the change in writing. Ask for the cancellation terms when you book so you have them from the start.

faq.q: Is the car in the photo the car I get?
faq.a: Yes. You book the exact car you see, by name. Every photograph on this site is of the car itself, taken at our office. If you would like a more recent photo, ask us and we will send it with your confirmation.

faq.q: Are the cars automatic?
faq.a: Nineteen of our twenty cars are automatic. The one manual is the Golf 5, which is also our cheapest car at 30 euro a day. On the mountain roads an automatic is worth having.

faq.q: Do you have a seven-seater?
faq.a: Yes, two of them, both Hyundai Santa Fe at 60 euro a day. They are a good choice for the Lake Koman ferry or the northern valleys with luggage.

faq.q: Which car should I take for the mountains?
faq.a: Take something with ground clearance. The Tucson or a Santa Fe handle the track into Theth and the last stretch to the Blue Eye. A low sedan is comfortable on the motorways and the coast road, though the rough final kilometres are hard work in one.

faq.q: Can I add a second driver or a child seat?
faq.a: Yes, both are common requests. Mention them in the same message as your dates and we will have them ready before you arrive, with the cost confirmed in writing.

faq.q: Which driving licence do I need?
faq.a: EU, UK and US licences are used here routinely. A licence printed in a non-Latin alphabet should come with an International Driving Permit, which you need to get in your own country before you travel. Please bring the physical card with you.

faq.q: What are the roads like?
faq.a: Better than their reputation. The SH1 north to Shkodër and the SH2 are motorway standard. The coast road over the Llogara pass and the routes into the north are narrow, steep, beautiful and slower than any map suggests, so allow extra time for them.

faq.q: Can I take the car to Kosovo, Montenegro or Greece?
faq.a: Crossing a border needs a green card insurance document prepared in advance, so please arrange it with us when you book rather than on the day. Ask us before you plan the route.

faq.q: Is parking difficult in Tirana?
faq.a: Central Tirana is busy and paid parking around the Blloku district fills up. Most hotels have an arrangement. Outside the capital, parking is rarely a problem at all.

faq.q: Anything about driving here I should know?
faq.a: Drive on the right. Headlights are expected outside towns, seatbelts are required, and the alcohol limit is effectively zero if you have held your licence under ten years. Expect livestock on rural roads outside the towns.

faq.q: Are you really open at 4am?
faq.a: Yes. Both offices are staffed around the clock, every day of the week, which is where our name comes from. Night arrivals from Istanbul and Rome are an ordinary part of our week.

faq.q: Where exactly do I meet you at the airport?
faq.a: Send your flight number with the booking and the meeting point comes back in your written confirmation, along with the name of the person who will be there.

faq.q: Can I collect at the airport and return in the city?
faq.a: Yes. The two offices are about ten minutes apart and using both is normal. Say which one you want for the return when you book.

faq.q: Can you deliver the car to my hotel?
faq.a: Inside Tirana this is a common arrangement. Ask when you book and it is confirmed in writing with any cost stated up front.

faq.q: How does fuel work?
faq.a: Ask us about the fuel arrangement when you book and we will put it in your written confirmation, so it is agreed before you drive away. The fuel stations nearest both offices are open through the night.

roads.name: The Albanian Riviera
roads.carWhy: A convertible is worth having on this road.
roads.story: The road climbs to a thousand metres at Llogara, turns a corner, and the whole Ionian coast opens up below you. It then drops through Dhërmi and Himarë to some of the clearest water in the country. This is the drive most of our customers come for.

roads.name: North to the Accursed Mountains
roads.best: June to September, closed in winter
roads.carWhy: The last hour into Theth needs ground clearance.
roads.story: The SH1 runs fast and flat to Shkodër, then the mountains begin. The final climb into Theth is a proper mountain pass, with a valley of stone houses at the end of it. Take a car with good ground clearance for this one.

roads.name: Berat and Gjirokastër
roads.carWhy: Long, smooth kilometres and plenty of room for luggage.
roads.story: Two Ottoman towns, both UNESCO listed, both built as rows of stone windows stacked up a hillside. The roads are easy the whole way, so this is a good route if you are new to driving in Albania.

destinations.name: Ksamil
destinations.carWhy: A long motorway run, so take something comfortable.
destinations.note: Three small islands close enough to swim to, in very clear, shallow water. June and September are the best months. In August the road in is slow and the beaches are full by nine.

destinations.name: The Blue Eye
destinations.carWhy: The last stretch is a rough track.
destinations.note: A deep spring that pushes cold, dark blue water up from underground. You park at the gate and walk the last kilometre. Swimming is discouraged, and the water sits at around ten degrees.

destinations.name: Butrint
destinations.carWhy: A short drive, and easy to park at the end.
destinations.note: Greek, Roman, Venetian and Ottoman ruins in a forest beside a lagoon, on the UNESCO list since 1992. Allow about two hours, and go early, before the tour buses arrive from Corfu.

destinations.name: Gjirokastër
destinations.carWhy: Hills all the way, and cobbles at the end.
destinations.note: The stone city, built in slate and shuttered windows up a steep hillside below a huge castle. The old town streets are steep and cobbled, so park lower down and walk up.

destinations.name: Lake Koman ferry
destinations.carWhy: Seven seats, and it takes the ferry with you.
destinations.note: A working ferry through a flooded canyon that many visitors compare to the fjords. Your car travels on the boat with you. Book the crossing ahead in summer.

destinations.name: Valbona valley
destinations.hours: 5 h, or via the Koman ferry
destinations.carWhy: Gravel and river crossings. Ground clearance matters.
destinations.note: Alpine valley at the top of the country, and the start of the Valbona to Theth walk if you have a spare day. Snowed in through winter, so June to September only.

destinations.name: Krujë
destinations.carWhy: Half a day out, and our cheapest car does it easily.
destinations.note: Skanderbeg's castle above an Ottoman bazaar of carpets and copper. The easiest real day trip from Tirana, and the one to do on your first afternoon while you get used to the roads.

destinations.name: Shkodër and Rozafa
destinations.carWhy: Fast, flat motorway the whole way.
destinations.note: A castle on a ridge where three rivers and a lake meet, and the best sunset view in northern Albania. The city below is flat, green and full of bicycles.

Tirana airport arrivals or the city office on Rruga Njazi Meka, about ten minutes apart. Both are staffed around the clock, so a 03:40 landing is an ordinary pickup for us. Give us your flight number and we will hold the car if you are late.

Return it to either office, whichever suits the end of your trip, at whatever hour your flight leaves. Tell us in advance if you want to change which one and we will confirm it in writing.
